source_refs.note: 1. Aeroplane Wings: a main subheading of 5.12 Uses of Bernoulli's principle, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 109-109.

blocks.text: The wing of an aeroplane is designed to deflect the air so that streamlines are closer together above the wing than below it as illustrated in Fig.5.17. We have seen that where the streamlines are forced closer together, the speed is faster. Thus, air is travelling faster on the upper side of the wing than on the lower. The pressure will be lower at the top of the wing, and the wing will be forced upward and the lift of an aeroplane is due to this effect.

blocks.alt: A side view of the rear of an aeroplane with a wing section in front of it. Green streamlines from the left crowd closely together over the curved upper surface of the wing and stay spread out below it, all moving to the right. Red arrows under the wing point upward.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.17: Lift of an aeroplane (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.17).
